tasks.question: How will life be different in fifty years' time?

models: It is possible that homes will become fully automated, and if this is the case, daily chores will require far less effort.
It is likely that people will live much longer lives, given that medical technology keeps advancing, and this suggests healthcare systems will need to adapt.
This could potentially lead to cities relying entirely on renewable energy, which might mean cleaner air for everyone.

cues.cue: robots / take over / many everyday tasks
models: One possible explanation is that robots will take over many everyday tasks, and this would account for a shorter working week.
There is a chance that populations will shift towards smart cities, although it is equally possible that rural areas will be revitalised instead.
This may be due to virtual reality replacing physical travel, which would explain why fewer people commute long distances, and if so cities may look very different.

tasks.question: How do you think we will travel in the future?

models: It is reasonable to suppose that electric vehicles will become the standard, given that battery technology keeps improving, and therefore petrol cars will gradually disappear.
It is likely that self-driving cars will replace human drivers, given that the technology is advancing rapidly, and this suggests road accidents may fall.
It can be assumed that flights will become more affordable, based on the fact that competition among airlines keeps growing, and new routes keep opening.
It is possible that hyperloop systems will connect major cities, and if this is the case, journey times could shrink dramatically.
This might result from drones being adapted for short-distance transport, which could explain a rise in urban air traffic, and if so cities will need new regulations.
This appears to suggest that public transport will expand significantly, which might mean fewer people owning private cars, although rural areas may see slower change.

tasks.question: How might schools change in the coming years?

models: It is possible that classrooms will rely more heavily on technology, and if this is the case, traditional teaching methods may fade.

cues.cue: students / learn / at their own pace
models: This could potentially lead to students learning at their own pace, which might mean personalised lessons for every learner.

cues.cue: artificial intelligence / support / teachers in the classroom
models: It is likely that artificial intelligence will support teachers in the classroom, given that the technology is developing quickly, and this suggests lesson planning will become more efficient.

cues.cue: exams / give way / to continuous assessment
models: One possible explanation is that exams will give way to continuous assessment, and this would account for less pressure on students.

cues.cue: remote learning / remain / a permanent option
models: It is reasonable to suppose that remote learning will remain a permanent option, given that many schools have already adopted it, and therefore flexibility will increase.

cues.cue: schools / focus / more on practical skills
models: This appears to suggest that schools will focus more on practical skills, which might mean graduates are better prepared for real jobs, although core subjects will likely remain.

tasks.question: What do you think cities will be like in the future?

models: This could potentially lead to cities growing even larger, which might mean greater pressure on housing and infrastructure.
It is likely that skyscrapers will dominate the skyline, given that land in cities keeps becoming scarcer, and this suggests vertical living will grow more common.

cues.cue: green spaces / become / more integrated into design
models: It is possible that green spaces will become more integrated into urban design, and if this is the case, cities may feel far less crowded.
One possible explanation is that traffic will largely disappear with autonomous transport, and this would account for shorter, calmer commutes.

cues.cue: smart systems / manage / energy and waste
models: It can be assumed that smart systems will manage energy and waste more efficiently, based on the fact that sustainability is a growing priority.
There is a chance that housing costs will rise even further, although it is equally possible that new building methods will ease the pressure.

tasks.question: How will technology change the way we work?

models: It is possible that remote work will become permanent, and if this is the case, office spaces may shrink considerably.
It is likely that artificial intelligence will automate many routine tasks, given how quickly the technology is developing, and this suggests some jobs will disappear entirely.
This may be due to industries changing so rapidly, which would explain why workers will need constant retraining, and if so lifelong learning will become essential.
One possible explanation is that four-day working weeks will become more common, and this would account for improved productivity and wellbeing.

cues.cue: virtual meetings / replace / most business travel
models: This might result from virtual meetings replacing most business travel, which could explain a sharp fall in flight bookings, and if so airlines will need to adapt.
It is reasonable to suppose that freelance work will grow in popularity, given that flexibility is increasingly valued, and therefore traditional employment may decline.

tasks.question: How do you think communication will develop in the future?

models: It is possible that holographic calls will replace video calls, and if this is the case, remote conversations will feel far more natural.
This could potentially lead to translation apps removing language barriers almost entirely, which might mean international communication becomes effortless.

cues.cue: social media / evolve / into more immersive platforms
models: This appears to suggest that social media will evolve into more immersive platforms, which might mean users spend even more time online, although privacy concerns may slow this down.

cues.cue: written messages / decline / in favour of voice notes
models: This may be due to voice notes becoming more convenient than typing, which would explain why written messages could decline, and if so communication will feel more personal.
It can be assumed that wearable devices will handle much of our everyday communication, based on the fact that smart technology keeps shrinking in size.

cues.cue: artificial intelligence / draft / most routine messages
models: It is reasonable to suppose that artificial intelligence will draft most routine messages, given current trends, and therefore people will spend less time on basic correspondence.
